_comment: DAY-STATE gate, SPENT branch only. FreshDayATR=0 is the off switch for the early-entry branch: dayStateOK guards it with `fresh > 0 &&`, so exactly 0 removes it entirely — a small positive value like 0.01 does NOT, it still admits a day whose range has barely opened. What is left is one strategy instead of two: buy the RSI pullback only after the day has already spent at least SpentDayATR of its daily ATR, i.e. the sell-off has happened. 5 evaluations. Compare its profit factor against cal_day.json (both branches) and against a fresh-only run (SpentDayATR far above any reachable range, e.g. 99) — a two-branch profit factor averages two different trades together and can hide that one branch pays for the other. Caveat: the gate lets the entry through when TodayHigh/TodayLow are missing, so a data hole reads as 'allowed', not as 'spent'. Run: go run ./cmd/backtest -ticker GAZP -strategy rsi_pullback -interval Minutes30 -calibrate data/params/rsi_pullback/cal_day_spent.json -out ./reports/GAZP_day_spent -months 24 -min-trades 20 -test-months 6 -metric profit_factor. GAZP is only the example instrument here: this file sweeps one theme and is ticker-agnostic, so replace -ticker and -out to calibrate another name (e.g. -ticker T -out ./reports/T_day_spent, adding -refresh on a ticker whose candle cache is short).
